Three subsequent pushes, a label change and a close/reopen all failed to trigger `CI/CD Pipeline`, while other PRs in the repo did get runs in the same window — this looks like an Actions scheduling problem on GitHub's side, not a change in this PR.

The two failures from run 31963592712 are fixed and verified locally:

- **File size limit** — `src/config.rs` (1046) and `src/gemini.rs` (1040) exceeded 1000 lines. Split into `src/upstream_client.rs` and `src/gemini/native.rs`; no file under `src/` now exceeds 1000 lines.
- **Coverage baseline** — measured locally with the same `cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7` the workflow pins: 78.867484% (up from the 78.180575% baseline on main), committed to `coverage-baseline.txt`, which keeps the ratchet unchanged within its 0.01 tolerance.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (zero warnings under `-D warnings`) and the full `cargo test` suite are clean at `64473d5`. Please re-run the pipeline when Actions picks up jobs again.

## 🔄 Auto-restart 1/5

**Reason:** Merge conflicts detected

Starting new session to address the issues.

---
*Auto-restart-until-mergeable mode is active. This run will stop after 5 restart iterations in total.*

Merged `main` (through #198) into this branch and resolved the conflicts. CI run [31967238520](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/31967238520) is green and the PR is now `MERGEABLE`/`CLEAN`.

Three files conflicted, but only one was a real semantic conflict:

**`tests/router_e2e/cases_regressions.rs`** — both branches appended tests to the same end of the file, so git interleaved them. Rebuilt from `main`'s version plus this branch's two tests; all tests from both branches survive.

**`src/output_limit.rs` behaviour change (the real conflict).** #186 replaced the router's *refusal* of `max_output_tokens` on Codex-backed surfaces with local emulation — the field is stripped before forwarding and the router truncates the answer itself. The native Gemini namespace added here routes cross-provider models through the same `proxy::openai_chat_completions` handler, so it inherits that emulation and can no longer refuse an output cap. `generate_content_reports_the_codex_output_limit_gap_natively` failed with `left: 200, right: 400`, correctly reporting the new behaviour rather than a merge mistake.

Reconciled by asserting the emulation instead, in `generate_content_emulates_the_output_cap_natively`: on **both** a Codex- and a Claude-owned model, a cap the answer fits into leaves it intact with `finishReason: "STOP"`, and a cap below it truncates with `finishReason: "MAX_TOKENS"`. This needed one stub change: the Anthropic stub ignored `max_tokens`. Anthropic genuinely enforces the cap upstream (only the ChatGPT backend rejects the field and needs the router's emulation), so the stub now honours it, counting one token per whitespace-separated word to stay consistent with the `output_tokens` it already reports.

**`coverage-baseline.txt`** — both branches had raised it independently (78.595261% on main, 78.867484% here). Re-measured the merged tree with the same `cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7` the workflow pins: **79.227252%**, above both, so neither side's pre-merge number would have kept the ratchet check idempotent.

Docs and the changelog fragment were updated to match, and the PR description now describes the merged behaviour. Full suite, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` are clean locally at `2a03173`.

The scope note stands unchanged: the Cursor CLI Connect-RPC adapter from #187 is still deliberately out of this PR (see "Not included" in the description), so #187 remains only partially addressed.
